findings.claim: The workbook contains three test-specific worksheets with literal matching Test ID and Test piece ID values: Vh5205_T-71, Vh5205_T-74 and Vh5205_T-84. Their respective F3 and F4 identifiers match the sheet name. The record description explains that these sheets contain individual-test selected results, while Common-to-all applies to the campaign. This supports within-document test pairing, not three statistically independent specimens, heats, batches or campaigns.

findings.claim: Each test sheet directly labels current-test proof strength Rp0.2 in MPa at row13, tensile strength Rm in MPa at row14, reduction of area Z in % at row15, total extension at maximum force Agt in % at row16 and plastic extension at maximum force Ag in % at row17. All five have stored literal numeric result strings in the same sheet. Proof level is anchored by Rp0.2 in C13, independently of the separate, blank room-temperature proof-strength entry in Common-to-all row65. No fitting, ranking or numeric interpretation was performed.

Common-to-all specifies CMSX-6, a temperature of 980 with the literal unit ℃, a tensile-test standard DIN EN ISO 6892-2:2018-09, and Method A rate control. These are documentary operating conditions. This independent XLSX evidence does not repair the earlier schema CSV encoding or its literal question-mark unit fields. Per-test actual rate and heating/soaking information is separately populated; no rate-unit conversion or temperature correction was applied.

After-fracture elongation A is not interchangeable with the reported Agt, Ag or Z. Common-to-all says the determination requirement for A was not met, describes fracture outside the extensometer gauge length and says final gauge length was not measurable. Those missing/inapplicable outcomes must remain distinct; no replacement label was constructed.

The retained record metadata states that expanded measurement uncertainty for Rm, Rp0.2 and Z was determined for each test, and Table1 reports maximum values at stated 95% confidence with k=2. Its percentage columns report 1.2 for Rm, 1.2 for Rp0.2 and max.0.5 for Z. These are publisher-reported campaign maxima, not workbook per-cell uncertainty budgets, prediction intervals, simultaneous coverage or independently recomputed results. The Z header combines percentage notation and an endpoint already measured in percent; no relative-to-absolute or percentage-point conversion is inferred.

findings.claim: No explicit per-test uncertainty budget, covariance matrix or coverage-factor fields were identified in the admitted workbook projection. A disclosed case-insensitive substring search of every projected cell value, formula text and ordinary comment found no uncert, covarian, correlat, coverage, confidence or standard deviation text. This is scoped documentary/lexical evidence, not a proof that unparsed parts, linked LIS data, standards or certificates lack such information. None of those linked bodies was requested.

The common sheet documents calibration status/class/standards and common equipment identifiers for the load, temperature and extension measurement chain. It defines engineering stress as force divided by original cross-sectional area and describes shared analysis procedures/software. These are provenance clues for possible shared errors; they do not quantify covariance or validate independent endpoint errors. Calibration certificate information cells are blank at the cited locations.

Temperature traceability is marked Yes, while the calibration correction is explicitly not included in indicated temperature. The primary-data description says indicated temperature was displayed but could not be recorded continuously. A calibration deviation value with K unit is present, but it is not an uncertainty or an automatically applicable correction. No time series or temperature correction was reconstructed.

Roughness uses the same full test identifiers, whereas the orientation sheet uses numeric specimen numbers 71,74,84 and points to Common-to-all row54. Those numeric suffixes were not silently normalized into full IDs. Common-to-all describes shared material preparation and test-piece history, but does not establish independent casts/heats or a sampling frame. A lexical absence of batch or heat number in projected values cannot resolve that lineage.

The two formula cells occur in Heat_treatment B24 and B25. Their text is consistent with a Celsius-to-Fahrenheit expression by inspection, but formulas, shared-formula attributes and stored caches were not executed or validated. No formula occurs in the three test result sheets. Numeric values and date serials remain source strings; styles were not rendered.

The next admissible use is exposed-reference engineering work with explicitly cited labels and missingness. The workbook supports documentary co-location of selected endpoints and provenance, but it does not supply an independently known covariance model or fresh predictive evaluation units. G20 uncertainty/lineage questions and G21 scientific evaluation design remain unresolved; no benchmark admission, criterion, model, allocation or fit follows from this acquisition.
